benchmark_progress: Production content builds now fail closed (BuildContentIntegrityError) instead of silently generating zero article slugs when Supabase retrieval fails, with a validated/integrity-checked snapshot fallback mechanism in place. No production snapshot is committed yet (no live Supabase credentials available in this environment) — populating it via `npm run content:snapshot` is a non-blocking follow-up for the owner; the fail-closed default is strictly safer than the prior silent-empty-array behavior in the meantime.
objective: Prevent a green production build from silently generating zero article slugs when Supabase content retrieval fails. Use a validated snapshot or fail closed.
summary: getBlogPosts()/getBlogPost() in lib/supabase-blog.ts caught every Supabase config/query/network error and returned []/null, so every build-time consumer (generateStaticParams for /blog/[slug], the blog/education/home listing pages, and app/sitemap.ts) treated a failed fetch identically to 'no articles yet.' A Supabase outage during `next build` could therefore ship a fully green deploy with zero article routes. Added lib/content-snapshot.ts (a committed, sha256-integrity-checked JSON snapshot loader) and scripts/export-content-snapshot.mjs (a read-only exporter an operator runs against a healthy Supabase connection to populate/refresh it). getBlogPosts()/getBlogPost() now use live data when available, fall back to the validated snapshot on failure or an unexpected empty result, and throw BuildContentIntegrityError when neither source has any content, overridable only via an explicit ALLOW_EMPTY_ARTICLE_BUILD=true escape hatch. Also removed a bare try/catch in app/sitemap.ts that was silently swallowing this exact class of error for sitemap generation.
